question: When you look at a standard X-ray, what color do dense structures like bones usually appear?
explanation: Bones block the X-ray beams from passing through to the film, creating a bright white picture. You've got this! [learn more](GNS123_U2_T10#GNS123_U2_T10_h1)

question: Why is it super helpful for nurses to understand basic X-ray imaging?

options.A: To replace the radiologist in reading films
options.B: To prescribe the correct radiation dosage
options.C: To operate the heavy X-ray machine safely
options.D: To help coordinate care and ease patient anxiety

explanation: As a nurse, you are the friendly face who prepares patients and calms their nerves before procedures. Great nursing starts with great communication! [learn more](GNS123_U2_T10#GNS123_U2_T10_h1)

question: What are the three golden rules of radiation safety?
explanation: Always remember: spend less time near radiation, step back to create distance, and use lead shielding. Safety first! [learn more](GNS123_U2_T10#GNS123_U2_T10_h2)

question: How does stepping further away from an active X-ray source affect your radiation exposure?
explanation: Radiation spreads out as it travels. The further away you stand, the safer you are! [learn more](GNS123_U2_T10#GNS123_U2_T10_h2)

question: What is a standard chest X-ray most commonly used to check for in the ward?

options.A: Viewing active blood flow inside brain tissue
options.B: Checking for pneumonia or heart enlargement
options.D: Detecting microscopic bacterial infections in blood

explanation: Chest X-rays give us a clear view of the lungs and heart size, making them perfect for spotting conditions like pneumonia. [learn more](GNS123_U2_T10#GNS123_U2_T10_h3)

question: A patient arrives at the clinic with severe lower right chest pain after a motorcycle fall. Which test is the doctor likely to order first?
explanation: After chest trauma, an X-ray is the quickest way to check for broken ribs or bruised lungs. You're building great clinical instincts! [learn more](GNS123_U2_T10#GNS123_U2_T10_h3)

question: Why do we ask patients to take off all jewelry and metallic objects before an X-ray?

options.A: They make the patient feel too heavy on the table
options.B: They attract stray electrical currents from the machine
options.C: They cause the X-ray tube to overheat quickly
options.D: They create dense white artifacts that hide details

explanation: Metal blocks X-rays completely, leaving bright white spots that might hide important clues on the film. [learn more](GNS123_U2_T10#GNS123_U2_T10_h4)

question: What is a vital safety question a nurse must ask a young female patient before a pelvic or abdominal X-ray?

options.A: Do you have a history of high blood pressure?
options.B: Have you ever had a blood transfusion?
options.D: What is your normal daily diet?

explanation: Radiation can harm a growing baby, so checking for pregnancy beforehand is a crucial safety step for every female of childbearing age. [learn more](GNS123_U2_T10#GNS123_U2_T10_h4)

question: Why are patients usually asked to hold their breath for a quick second during a chest X-ray?

options.A: To prevent radiation from entering the stomach
options.B: To prevent motion blur and clearly view lung fields
options.C: To lower their blood pressure during the flash
options.D: To make the heart beat slower for the picture

explanation: Breathing makes the chest move, which blurs the picture. Holding still gives us a crystal-clear image! [learn more](GNS123_U2_T10#GNS123_U2_T10_h5)

question: Which of these is NOT a normal nursing duty when taking a patient for an X-ray?

options.A: Monitoring oxygen therapy levels during transport
options.B: Developing the X-ray films in the darkroom
options.C: Explaining positioning steps to calm the patient
options.D: Ensuring intravenous lines have adequate slack

explanation: Developing films is the job of the radiographer, while keeping the patient safe and comfortable is your superpower as a nurse! [learn more](GNS123_U2_T10#GNS123_U2_T10_h5)

question: How do hospitals keep imaging going during sudden power outages?

options.A: Utilizing backup generators and battery-powered portable units
options.B: Performing manual sketches of internal organs at the bedside
options.C: Canceling all diagnostic imaging tests for the entire week
options.D: Waiting indefinitely until the public electricity grid restores power

explanation: Backup generators and portable machines are lifesavers when the main power grid goes down in clinical settings. [learn more](GNS123_U2_T10#GNS123_U2_T10_h6)

question: You are in a busy radiology department with a stable routine patient and an emergency trauma patient who is struggling to breathe. Who gets imaged first?

options.A: Prioritize the unstable trauma patient for immediate imaging
options.B: Send both patients in together to save time
options.C: Tell the trauma patient to wait in the normal queue
options.D: Cancel both appointments and reschedule for next month

explanation: Emergency and unstable patients always come first so we can catch and treat life-threatening issues right away. [learn more](GNS123_U2_T10#GNS123_U2_T10_h6)
